title: Riya' sort and sharing guide
subject: Islamic Studies
source: Seeded from islamic-studies/y8 lesson 29 (Pupil PDF worksheet: riya' sort and sharing guide)
intro: Lesson 29: The opposite of ikhlas: riya' and seeking praise. To understand riya' (showing off), why it is dangerous and how a Muslim guards against it

cards: Praying the same alone or seen
Giving more because the list is public
blocks.title: Sort into: Danger of riya' / Not riya'
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Danger of riya', Not riya'.
blocks.answer: Danger of riya': Lengthening salah because guests watch; Giving more because the list is public; Posting charity for likes. Not riya': Praying the same alone or seen; Teaching a sibling to pray; Feeling glad when praised afterwards

questions.q: Explain why riya' is so dangerous. (4 marks, our own question)
questions.a: It empties great deeds of reward, as in the hadith of the three judged first (Muslim); it is minor shirk; it is hidden and hard to notice.
questions.model: Point 1: it removes reward. Develop: the fighter, scholar and donor got only people's praise (Muslim). Point 2: it is a form of minor shirk. Develop: the deed is shared between Allah and people.

questions.q: Doing deeds so people hear of them is ...
Write a short guide in the portal response box: 'Five ways to post or share good deeds without losing ikhlas', with a reason for each and one evidence. Start: 'Before you post, ask yourself ...'
questions.a: Check intention, share to teach not to boast, keep most deeds secret, du'a, stop if the heart changes; hadith of the three or 98:5
questions.model: Teacher writes tip 1: 'Before you post, ask yourself: would I still do this if no one saw it?'

questions.q: what is 'ujb and how is it different from riya'?
questions.a: 'Ujb is admiring yourself; riya' is seeking others' praise

questions.q: Back to our ponder: inspiring or showing off?
questions.a: It depends on the intention; guard the heart
